slides.prompt: std::list is a doubly linked list while std::forward_list is a singly linked list. Both offer O(1) constant time insertion and deletion anywhere once an iterator is obtained.

slides.title: Random Access in std::list
slides.prompt: Can you access elements in std::list using operator[] or indexing?
options: No, std::list supports only bidirectional step-by-step traversal via iterators
Yes, operator[] is available with O(1) complexity
Yes, operator[] is available with O(log N) complexity
Only if the list is sorted
slides.correctAnswer: No, std::list supports only bidirectional step-by-step traversal via iterators

slides.title: std::forward_list Efficiency
slides.prompt: What advantage does std::forward_list have over std::list?
options: Lower memory overhead per element since each node stores only a single next pointer
slides.correctAnswer: Lower memory overhead per element since each node stores only a single next pointer

slides.title: Splice Operations
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function used to transfer elements between std::list containers without copying.

slides.title: Iterator Invalidation on Insertion
slides.prompt: What happens to existing iterators in std::list when a new element is inserted?
options: Iterators remain valid because memory nodes are heap-allocated independently
Iterators after the insertion point are invalidated
slides.correctAnswer: Iterators remain valid because memory nodes are heap-allocated independently

slides.title: Inserting in forward_list
slides.prompt: Fill in the insertion method used for forward_list that inserts after a specified iterator position.

slides.title: std::list::sort Method
slides.prompt: Why should you use member function 'lst.sort()' instead of 'std::sort(lst.begin(), lst.end())'?
options: std::sort requires random access iterators which std::list does not provide
std::sort converts list to vector internally causing extra memory usage
std::list cannot be sorted under any circumstances
slides.correctAnswer: std::sort requires random access iterators which std::list does not provide
